title: Wounds, Rifts, and Wars
coreMove: Preserve the reality of a wound without turning innocence into group property that licenses the next harm.
sourcePressure: The group-conflict chapter scales self-justification into us-versus-them thinking, selective collective memory, grievance as identity, retaliation loops, and loyalty costs around self-examination.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Equating all harms, flattening historical injuries, or jumping to conflict-resolution optimism instead of showing how grievance becomes self-renewing identity.

sourceAnchors.name: us-versus-them escalation
sourceAnchors.detail: the source supports the pattern in which each group justifies its own behavior while reading the other side as the real aggressor
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Each side can call its own blow context and the other side's blow character.

sourceAnchors.name: injury as identity
sourceAnchors.detail: the source supports grievance becoming central to what a group believes it is
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A wound can remain true and still become the passport a group uses to cross into retaliation.

hook: Do not open with a named war or current political conflict.
Avoid flags, battlefields, and casualty imagery.
counterintuition: Do not imply real wounds should be forgotten.
examples: No family argument reused from ch7.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective realization, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a union-management safety committee after a bruising lockout
exampleSpecs.audience: workplace groups carrying institutional memory into negotiations
exampleSpecs.stakes: a new guardrail dispute may become proof that the other side never changes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan separates the lockout wound from the current guardrail defect before the committee votes to retaliate procedurally
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dented safety guard laid across a bargaining-room credenza

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood redevelopment forum between long-time residents and new apartment owners
exampleSpecs.audience: civic groups whose identity is built around being harmed or ignored
exampleSpecs.stakes: a zoning meeting becomes a ritual of accusation rather than a decision about one block
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivier maps who lost what in the last project and who would bear costs now, preventing either side from using one wound as the whole map
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a foam-board zoning map propped on a scratched folding table

exampleSpecs.domain: an online fan community split after moderators banned a popular contributor
exampleSpecs.audience: community leaders watching grievance turn into identity badges
exampleSpecs.stakes: every moderation decision becomes evidence of betrayal or chaos
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marit predicts both factions' interpretation of the same moderation log, then posts the rule breach and the process miss together
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a moderation queue glowing on a laptop in a dark spare room

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional school merger committee balancing two towns with a long rivalry
exampleSpecs.audience: public officials handling inherited group memory
exampleSpecs.stakes: bus routes and mascot choices become carriers for older humiliation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sam reads the old closure minutes and the current enrollment numbers in the same meeting before letting either town claim pure victimhood
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a faded school mascot patch taped beside an enrollment chart

exampleSpecs.domain: a museum repatriation working group after a disputed exhibit label
exampleSpecs.audience: institutions and community representatives balancing truth, injury, and defensiveness
exampleSpecs.stakes: one side may treat any admission as betrayal while the other treats any delay as denial
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It takes Javier two drafts to write a label that names the institution's acquisition choice without asking the harmed group to soften the wound
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blank exhibit label held under a strip of gallery track lighting

exampleSpecs.domain: a refugee association board split between older arrivals and newly arrived families
exampleSpecs.audience: community groups where past survival can become current gatekeeping
exampleSpecs.stakes: aid allocation becomes a moral contest over who suffered correctly
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Adaeze write two true sentences: what the older group endured, and what that history does not entitle them to deny newcomers
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stack of translated intake forms weighted by a chipped ceramic paperweight

skillTargets: separate real injury from identity that licenses retaliation
analyze how loyalty polices collective memory
choose moves that name one's own group's aggression without denying the wound

tryThisNowSpec: For one group you belong to, write two true sentences: what was done to us, and what that does not give us permission to do now.
